newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu to study Chile copper smelter.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu to study Chile copper smelter.

text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy said in a statement on Wednesday that the Outokumpu-Endesa consortium had signed a contract to conduct a feasibility study of a copper smelter-refinery project in Chile.
"Outokumpu and Endesa are proceeding with their plans to have a big greenfield copper smelter-refinery built at Mejillones in northern Chile," Outokumpu said.

The contract signed with Davy International was "for the preparation of a bankable feasibility study for the project," it said. The plant is expected to produce 350,000 tonnes of cathode copper per year. The investment cost is $800 million," it said.
The study would be started immediately and was expected to be completed in July.
"Outokumpu-Endesa will next proceed to contact Chilean concentrate producers for negotiations to secure raw material for the smelter," Outokumpu said.
Presuming that the feasibility study gave the go-ahead, Outokumpu said the consortium would "take additional partners to join the project as minority shareholders."
Construction could start in late 1998 and copper cathode production could commence in the second half of 2000, it said.
